en.statement: A method's local `int n;` declaration gives `n` the default value zero.
en.explanation: A local int variable needs definite assignment before a read; its declaration alone supplies no value.

en.statement: Adding two `int` values throws ArithmeticException when the mathematical sum exceeds the `int` range.
en.explanation: An overflowing int sum wraps within the int range; integer overflow itself raises no exception.

en.statement: `-7 / 3` evaluates to `-2` because integer division truncates toward zero.
en.explanation: Integer division rounds a negative quotient toward zero, giving -2 for -7 divided by 3.

en.statement: A `char` value represents an unsigned 16-bit UTF-16 code unit.
en.explanation: Java's char stores one UTF-16 code unit; a supplementary Unicode character occupies two such units.

en.statement: `short s = 1; s += 1;` compiles because `+=` includes a conversion back to `short`.
en.explanation: Compound assignment converts the addition's result back to the short variable's type.

en.statement: `Double.NaN == Double.NaN` evaluates to `true`.
en.explanation: Floating-point == returns false when either operand is NaN, even when both operands are Double.NaN.

en.statement: Unboxing a null Integer reference throws NullPointerException.
en.explanation: Unboxing needs the wrapper's primitive value. A null Integer reference triggers NullPointerException during that conversion.

en.statement: With `Integer a = 127, b = 127;`, `a == b` evaluates to `true`.
en.explanation: The JLS guarantees identical references when the same integer constant in the range -128 to 127 is boxed.

en.statement: `Integer.valueOf(1).equals(Long.valueOf(1))` returns `true`.
en.explanation: Integer.equals requires its argument to be an Integer holding the same int value. A Long argument yields false.

en.statement: Given overloads `f(long)` and `f(Integer)`, the call `f(1)` selects `f(Integer)`.
en.explanation: f(1) selects f(long): primitive widening matches before overload resolution considers boxing.

en.statement: For an ArrayList<Integer> containing 1, `remove(Integer.valueOf(1))` removes its first matching element.
en.explanation: An Integer argument selects List.remove(Object), which removes the first occurrence equal to that argument.

en.statement: In Java 25, the Integer(int) constructor carries a deprecation marked for removal.
en.explanation: Java 25 declares Integer(int) as @Deprecated(since="9"), with no forRemoval flag.

en.statement: Calling `replace` on a String writes the replacement characters into that String.
en.explanation: String.replace returns its result while leaving the receiver's characters unchanged.

en.statement: `"tr" + "ue" == "true"` is true because the concatenation is a constant expression.
en.explanation: The constant concatenation "tr" + "ue" denotes the interned String "true", so the references match.

en.statement: After `String p = "tr";`, `(p + "ue") == "true"` compares the same interned String instance.
en.explanation: Run-time concatenation with non-final p creates a new String whose reference differs from the literal "true".

en.statement: `final String p = "tr";` makes a local `p` usable in String constant expressions.
en.explanation: A final String local initialized with a constant expression is a constant variable and can participate in constant expressions.

en.statement: `"go".equals(new String("go"))` compares the identity of the String objects.
en.explanation: String.equals compares character content. Both String objects contain "go", so this call returns true.

en.statement: A String switch matches `case "go"` when its selector is `new String("go")`.
en.explanation: A String switch compares its selector with String case constants using String.equals, so matching text selects that case.

source.title: JLS 25 §14.11.1.2: Determining the Applicable Switch Label

en.statement: For distinct StringBuilder objects holding "go", the call `equals` returns `false`.
en.explanation: StringBuilder.equals checks builder identity rather than character content, so matching text leaves distinct builders unequal.

en.statement: `"\u2003x\u2003".trim()` returns `"x"` by removing the surrounding Unicode white space.
en.explanation: String.trim removes characters whose values are at most U+0020. The U+2003 EM SPACE characters remain around "x".

en.statement: The compiler requires a line terminator after a text block's opening triple quotes.
en.explanation: A text block opening consists of triple quotes, optional horizontal white space, and a line terminator before the content.

en.statement: A text block preserves unescaped trailing spaces at the ends of its content lines.
en.explanation: Text block processing strips trailing white space from content lines.

source.title: Java SE 25 Text Blocks Programmer's Guide

en.statement: The compiler normalizes CRLF line endings in text block source content to LF.
en.explanation: Text block processing converts source CRLF and CR line terminators to LF before interpreting escapes.

en.statement: In a text block, backslash followed by a line terminator inserts a newline into the String.
en.explanation: The backslash-line-terminator escape suppresses that source line break in a text block's String value.

en.statement: Object.equals compares the values of an object's fields when the class inherits that method.
en.explanation: Inherited Object.equals returns true for two references to the same object; it does not inspect fields.

en.statement: The equals contract specifies agreement between `a.equals(b)` and `b.equals(a)` for non-null references.
en.explanation: Symmetry requires both directions of an equals comparison between non-null references to give the same result.

en.statement: Under the equals contract, `x.equals(y)` may alternate results while both objects' state stays fixed.
en.explanation: The equals contract requires repeated comparisons of the same objects to agree while equality-related information stays unchanged.

en.statement: Equal objects return matching hash codes under the hashCode contract.
en.explanation: Objects equal according to equals must produce the same hashCode result.

en.statement: The hashCode contract requires unequal objects to return distinct hash codes.
en.explanation: Unequal objects may share a hash code; the hashCode contract permits collisions.

en.statement: The Map contract specifies stable lookup after a key changes in a way that affects equals.
en.explanation: Changing equality-related state while an object is a Map key puts the map's behavior outside its specified guarantees.

en.statement: `Objects.hash("x")` returns the same hash code as `"x".hashCode()`.
en.explanation: Objects.hash computes an array-style hash for its arguments, which differs from "x".hashCode() for this single argument.

en.statement: With distinct arrays `int[] a = {1}, b = {1};`, the call `a.equals(b)` returns `false`.
en.explanation: An array's equals checks its reference identity; these separately created arrays are unequal despite their matching elements.

en.statement: A naturally ordered TreeSet keeps BigDecimal values `4.0` and `4.00` as one element.
en.explanation: BigDecimal's natural ordering treats 4.0 and 4.00 as equivalent, so a naturally ordered TreeSet retains a single element.

en.statement: A subclass static method with the same signature as a superclass static method overrides it.
en.explanation: The subclass method hides the superclass one: a call through a superclass-typed reference still runs the superclass's static method, because the compile-time type picks a class method.

en.statement: A virtual instance method call chooses an override using the receiver's runtime class.
en.explanation: Virtual method lookup selects an override from the receiver's runtime class hierarchy.

en.statement: A class executes its instance field initializers before executing its superclass constructor.
en.explanation: A class executes its instance field initializers after its superclass constructor returns.

source.title: JLS 25 §12.5: Creation of New Class Instances

en.statement: A superclass-typed reference selects an accessible superclass field that its runtime class hides.
en.explanation: Field lookup uses the expression's compile-time type, selecting the accessible superclass field.

source.title: JLS 25 §15.11.1: Field Access Using a Primary

en.statement: `class A{void f(Object x){}} class B extends A{@Override void f(String x){}}` compiles.
en.explanation: The subclass's f(String) overloads f(Object), so @Override makes this declaration a compile-time error.

en.statement: Declaring an array reference final makes assignments to its array elements compile-time errors.
en.explanation: A final array reference cannot be reassigned, but its array elements remain assignable.

en.statement: An inner member class instance has an immediately enclosing instance of its outer class.
en.explanation: A non-static member class is an inner class; its instance is associated with an instance of the enclosing class.

en.statement: The default constructor of a package-private class has public access.
en.explanation: A normal class's default constructor has its class's access level; for a package-private class, that access is package access.

en.statement: The compiler inserts `super()` into an empty constructor body in an ordinary subclass.
en.explanation: An empty ordinary subclass constructor implicitly invokes the direct superclass's no-argument constructor.

en.statement: In Java 25, a constructor prologue may assign to its class's field declared as `int x;`.
en.explanation: A Java 25 constructor prologue permits writes to same-class fields that have no initializer, including this.field assignments.

en.statement: Reassigning a method's reference parameter changes the reference stored in the caller's variable.
en.explanation: A method parameter receives a copy of the argument's reference value; reassigning that parameter leaves the caller's variable unchanged.

en.statement: An implementing class inherits static methods declared by its interfaces.
en.explanation: An interface's static methods belong to that interface; a class implementation inherits none of them.

en.statement: A public concrete instance method inherited from a class's superclass wins over a matching interface default.
en.explanation: A class does not inherit an interface default when a concrete method inherited from its superclass already has a matching signature, so the superclass method is the one that runs.

en.statement: A class resolves conflicting interface defaults using the order of its implements clause.
en.explanation: Matching defaults from unrelated interfaces create a compile-time conflict. The class resolves it by overriding the method.

en.statement: An interface declaring `default String toString() { return "x"; }` compiles.
en.explanation: An interface's default toString implementation produces a compile-time error because it matches a non-private Object method.

en.statement: An interface field declaration such as `int LIMIT = 10;` declares a public static final field.
en.explanation: Java supplies public, static and final for interface fields when their declarations omit those modifiers.

en.statement: An enum class may declare its constructor with the `protected` access modifier.
en.explanation: Java rejects protected enum constructors at compile time. Enum constructors use private access, explicitly or implicitly.

en.statement: An enum with a constant-specific class body is implicitly sealed.
en.explanation: An enum constant's class body declares an anonymous subclass; those subclasses form the enum's permitted set.

en.statement: `Status.values()` returns the constants of enum Status in their declaration order.
en.explanation: The compiler supplies values() for an enum. Its returned array follows the order of the constants in the enum declaration.

en.statement: `record Point(int x) {}` supplies a public accessor named `x()`.
en.explanation: A record's generated accessor uses its component's name as the method name and returns that component's value.

source.title: Record Classes – Java SE 25 Language Guide

en.statement: A compact record constructor assigns component fields after its body finishes normally.
en.explanation: The compiler uses the component parameters' resulting values to initialize the fields after a compact constructor's body.

en.statement: `record Box(List<String> items) {}` copies the supplied list in its generated canonical constructor.
en.explanation: The generated Box constructor stores the supplied list reference. Copying a mutable component requires an explicit constructor implementation.

en.statement: Generated equals for `record Data(int[] values) {}` compares the array elements.
en.explanation: The generated Data.equals method compares its values components by reference. Equal array contents alone do not make two Data records equal.

en.statement: A direct subclass of a sealed class requires one of `final`, `sealed`, or `non-sealed`.
en.explanation: A direct subclass has one of these modifiers explicitly or implicitly. Its status controls whether developers can extend its branch.

en.statement: In the unnamed module, a sealed class and its permitted direct subclasses may occupy different packages.
en.explanation: In the unnamed module, a permitted direct subclass belongs to the same package as its sealed superclass.

en.statement: A sealed class may infer its permitted direct subclasses from declarations in the same compilation unit.
en.explanation: When a sealed class omits a permits clause, Java infers eligible direct subclasses declared in that compilation unit.

en.statement: In a void method with `Object o`, `s` is in scope after `if (!(o instanceof String s)) return;`.
en.explanation: A guard that returns when an instanceof String pattern fails leaves its binding variable in scope for the following statements.

en.statement: With `record Box(Object x) {}`, `new Box(new Box("x"))` matches `Box(Box(String s))`.
en.explanation: Nested record patterns match component values recursively. The outer Box holds a Box whose component is a String, so the pattern binds s to "x".

en.statement: A switch statement with arrow labels continues into the next arm after the chosen arm completes.
en.explanation: An arrow-label switch executes the selected arm and then exits the switch when that arm completes normally.

en.statement: `case String s` is a valid label after an unguarded `case CharSequence cs` in the same switch.
en.explanation: The compiler rejects a String pattern after an unguarded CharSequence pattern because the preceding pattern already covers its matching values.

en.statement: An enum switch statement with just enum-constant arrow cases requires exhaustiveness to pass compilation.
en.explanation: An enum switch statement with just constant labels can omit constants. An omitted constant makes the statement complete normally without executing an arm.

source.title: JLS 25 §14.11.2: The Switch Block of a switch Statement

en.statement: A switch expression can cover a sealed interface exhaustively using its permitted-subtype type patterns.
en.explanation: Type-pattern cases covering a sealed selector's permitted subtypes provide exhaustive type coverage, so a default label is optional.

en.statement: For `String s = null;`, `switch (s) { default -> {} }` completes normally.
en.explanation: For a null String selector, a switch with a plain default label throws NullPointerException. That label does not match null.

en.statement: Since Java 22, a later expression can read the value of `String _ = "x";` by using `_`.
en.explanation: The underscore declares an unnamed variable but does not name it. An expression that tries to read that variable through _ is a compile-time error.

en.statement: A variable declared as `List<int>` holds a list parameterized with primitive int.
en.explanation: Java rejects List<int> at compile time because a concrete generic type argument is a reference type.

source.title: JLS SE 25 §4.5.1: Type Arguments of Parameterized Types

en.statement: A `List<Integer>` value is assignable to a variable of type `List<Number>`.
en.explanation: Java rejects assigning a List<Integer> to a List<Number> variable. A subtype relationship between element classes does not transfer to these parameterized types.

source.title: JLS 25 §4.10.2: Subtyping among Class and Interface Types

en.statement: With `Number[] xs = new Integer[1];`, `xs[0] = 1.5` throws ArrayStoreException.
en.explanation: The array's actual component type is Integer. The Double value from 1.5 fails the run-time array store check.

en.statement: Assigning a raw `List` to `List<String>` produces an unchecked warning.
en.explanation: The unchecked conversion means the compiler cannot verify that the raw list contains String values.

en.statement: The expression `new T()` compiles when `T` is a class type parameter.
en.explanation: Java rejects new T() at compile time. A type parameter identifies an unknown type rather than a class whose constructor the expression can invoke.

source.title: JLS SE 25 §15.9.1: Determining the Class being Instantiated

en.statement: Java creates an array of parameterized lists with `new List<String>[10]`.
en.explanation: Java rejects new List<String>[10] at compile time because array creation requires a component type available for run-time checking.

en.statement: Java treats `m(List<String>)` and `m(List<Integer>)` as distinct overloads in one class.
en.explanation: Both method declarations erase to m(List), so Java rejects the pair with a compile-time name-clash error.

source.title: JLS 25 §8.4.8.3: Requirements in Overriding and Hiding

en.statement: The objects from `new ArrayList<String>()` and `new ArrayList<Integer>()` share a run-time class.
en.explanation: Both constructions create ArrayList objects. Their generic type arguments do not produce separate run-time classes.

source.title: JLS 25 §8.1.2: Generic Classes and Type Parameters

en.statement: Inside a static method of `class Box<T>`, a local variable can be declared with the class's type parameter `T`.
en.explanation: A class's type parameter may not be named in a static context such as a static method body, where no current instance exists, so a local variable of type T there is a compile-time error.

en.statement: For a `List<? extends Number> xs`, `xs.add(null)` compiles.
en.explanation: The wildcard captures an unknown Number subtype. The null type is compatible with that captured reference type.

en.statement: For a `List<? super Integer> xs`, `xs.add(Integer.valueOf(4))` compiles.
en.explanation: A lower bound of Integer makes an Integer value valid for add, even though the list's exact element type is unknown.

en.statement: A reference typed as Map fits a parameter declared as Collection through interface inheritance.
en.explanation: Map and Collection have separate interface hierarchies. Java rejects passing a Map-typed reference as a Collection argument.

en.statement: Calling `put(null, "v")` on a HashMap stores a mapping under the null key.
en.explanation: HashMap permits the null key, so put can associate it with the value "v".

en.statement: A HashSet's insertion order determines its specified iteration order.
en.explanation: HashSet specifies no iteration order; its order may change over time.

en.statement: In an access-order LinkedHashMap, `get` places an existing entry last in encounter order.
en.explanation: In access-order mode, LinkedHashMap orders entries from least to most recently accessed; get counts as an access.

en.statement: TreeSet.addFirst inserts its argument at the start of the set's encounter order.
en.explanation: TreeSet.addFirst throws UnsupportedOperationException because comparison determines element positions.

en.statement: LinkedHashSet.addFirst puts an existing element first in the set's encounter order.
en.explanation: LinkedHashSet.addFirst relocates an existing element when necessary to make it first.

en.statement: `List.of("a", null)` throws NullPointerException while creating the list.
en.explanation: List.of rejects null elements during construction, so this call fails with NullPointerException.

en.statement: `Set.of("a", "a")` creates a single-element set by merging its duplicate arguments.
en.explanation: Set.of rejects duplicate elements with IllegalArgumentException.

en.statement: A list returned by Collections.unmodifiableList reflects changes made to its backing list.
en.explanation: Collections.unmodifiableList answers queries through its backing list, so updates made to that list remain visible.

en.statement: `Arrays.asList("a").add("b")` appends "b" to the returned list.
en.explanation: Arrays.asList returns a fixed-size list. Its add operation throws UnsupportedOperationException.

en.statement: The ArrayList API promises ConcurrentModificationException for cross-thread structural changes.
en.explanation: ArrayList iterators detect concurrent modification on a best-effort basis; ConcurrentModificationException is not guaranteed.

en.statement: An interface's public abstract equals(Object) method is excluded from its functional-interface method count.
en.explanation: Java excludes declarations matching public Object methods when identifying an interface's functional method, including an abstract equals(Object) declaration.

en.statement: A standalone lambda expression infers a functional interface from its parameter and return types.
en.explanation: A lambda gets its functional interface type from its assignment, invocation or cast context. Its body alone supplies no target interface.

source.title: JLS 25 §15.27.3 Type of a Lambda Expression

en.statement: The compiler checks that a lambda's captured local `int n = 1;` stays effectively final.
en.explanation: A lambda that reads a captured local still imposes the effectively final restriction. Reassigning that local elsewhere in the method breaks it.

en.statement: Within an instance method, a lambda's `this` refers to the lambda's own function object.
en.explanation: Inside a lambda body, this has its meaning from the enclosing context. In an enclosing instance method, it refers to that method's receiver.

en.statement: `String::length` uses the function's first argument as the String receiver.
en.explanation: String::length is an unbound instance-method reference. Invoking its functional method supplies the String whose length method runs.

source.title: JLS 25 §15.13.3: Run-Time Evaluation of Method References

en.statement: `Comparator.comparingInt(Person::age).thenComparing(Person::name).reversed()` orders ages ascending.
en.explanation: Calling reversed() on the composed Comparator reverses its complete ordering. The age comparison therefore runs in descending order.

en.statement: `var value = null;` declares a local variable whose static type is Object.
en.explanation: Java rejects a var declaration initialized with null at compile time because a local variable's inferred type cannot be the null type.

source.title: JLS 25 §14.4.1: Local Variable Declarators and Types

en.statement: `Function<String, String> f = (var s) -> s.trim();` gives the parameter s the type String.
en.explanation: A var lambda parameter gets its type from the target functional interface. Function<String, String> gives s the inferred type String.

source.title: Local Variable Type Inference – Java SE 25

en.statement: `try (var r = acquire()) {}` is a valid header when acquire() declares AutoCloseable as its return type.
en.explanation: A try-with-resources header permits var in a resource's declaration. The initializer supplies the resource variable's inferred type.

source.title: Local Variable Type Inference – Java SE 25

en.statement: `var first = 1, second = 2;` infers a separate static type for both local variables.
en.explanation: A var declaration containing multiple variable declarators is a compile-time error. Declare first and second in separate statements.

en.statement: Creating a stream's `filter` stage defers predicate calls until pipeline traversal.
en.explanation: filter is an intermediate operation. Creating its stage leaves the predicate waiting until a terminal operation begins traversal.

en.statement: A consumed Stream starts a new traversal when its caller invokes another terminal operation.
en.explanation: A Stream is consumed after a terminal operation. Reuse violates its contract; an implementation may throw IllegalStateException.

en.statement: For a stream with elements, the Stream API guarantees `peek` action execution during `count()`.
en.explanation: A stream implementation may skip peek when its side effects leave the terminal result unchanged, so a count pipeline may finish with no peek calls.

en.statement: `Stream.of(Stream.of("a", "b")).flatMap(s -> s).toList()` returns a list containing two String elements.
en.explanation: flatMap replaces an input element with elements from its mapper's stream. Mapping the inner stream to itself exposes its two strings.

en.statement: `Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)` keeps the last value when input elements produce duplicate keys.
en.explanation: The two-argument Collectors.toMap collector throws IllegalStateException when mapped keys collide; it supplies no implicit replacement policy.

en.statement: The Stream API guarantees that `Stream.toList()` rejects an attempt to add an element.
en.explanation: Stream.toList returns an unmodifiable list. Adding an element to that result throws UnsupportedOperationException.

en.statement: For an ordered parallel stream, `forEach` preserves element order in calls to its action.
en.explanation: A parallel Stream's forEach action calls have unspecified order, even when the source defines an encounter order.

en.statement: Since Java 24, `Stream.of(1,2,3,4).gather(Gatherers.windowSliding(3)).toList()` yields [[1,2,3],[2,3,4]].
en.explanation: windowSliding advances a full window by one element. With inputs 1 through 4 and size 3, the two windows share 2 and 3.

en.statement: `Optional.of(null)` returns an Optional instance that represents an absent value.
en.explanation: Optional.of requires a non-null value. Passing null throws NullPointerException.

en.statement: Calling `orElse(fallback())` evaluates `fallback()` even when the Optional holds a value.
en.explanation: Java evaluates method arguments before entering the method. An expression supplied to Optional.orElse runs even when the Optional already holds a value.

en.statement: The Optional API note names object fields as the main intended use for representing a missing value.
en.explanation: The Optional API note describes Optional as "primarily intended for use as a method return type" when a result may be absent.

en.statement: Java classifies subclasses of RuntimeException as checked exception types.
en.explanation: RuntimeException and its subclasses are unchecked exception classes. This classification includes NullPointerException and IllegalArgumentException.

en.statement: Java treats an IOException catch after an Exception catch in the same try as reachable.
en.explanation: In one try statement, a catch for Exception already covers IOException. The compiler rejects a later IOException catch because the earlier handler catches that type.

en.statement: For `catch (IOException | IllegalArgumentException e)`, the compiler rejects `e = null`.
en.explanation: A parameter declared by a multi-catch clause is implicitly final. Assigning a replacement reference to that parameter is a compile-time error.

en.statement: A finally block that completes with return discards a pending exception from the try block.
en.explanation: When a finally block completes with return, that return replaces the pending exception. The method returns rather than propagating that exception.

source.title: JLS 25 §14.20.2: Execution of try-finally and try-catch-finally

en.statement: AutoCloseable.close() declares Exception in its throws clause.
en.explanation: AutoCloseable declares close() with throws Exception. Its declared exception type covers failures a resource reports when releasing its resources.

en.statement: A try-with-resources statement closes its resources in reverse initialization order.
en.explanation: The try-with-resources closing order runs from the most recently initialized resource back to the earliest one.

en.statement: A try-with-resources statement runs its catch block before it closes its resources.
en.explanation: Try-with-resources attempts to close its resources before entering a catch block attached to the same statement.

en.statement: A null try-with-resources resource triggers NullPointerException during closing.
en.explanation: Try-with-resources skips closing a resource whose value is null. A null resource by itself does not cause an exception during automatic cleanup.

en.statement: An override replaces its parent's `throws IOException` clause with `throws Exception`.
en.explanation: An overriding method's checked exception declarations must stay within the inherited method's declared exception types. Exception is broader than IOException, so that replacement is rejected.

source.title: JLS 25 §8.4.8.3: Requirements in Overriding and Hiding

en.statement: An enclosing method's `throws IOException` covers an IOException escaping a `Function` lambda.
en.explanation: The compiler checks a lambda's checked exceptions against its target interface method. Function.apply declares no checked exceptions, so an enclosing throws IOException clause does not cover the lambda body.

en.statement: For a Runnable task, `new Thread(task).run()` starts another thread to execute task.
en.explanation: A direct run() call on a Thread created with a Runnable executes that task on the calling thread.

en.statement: A normal return from `join()` on a started Thread means that thread has terminated.
en.explanation: The untimed join method waits for a started thread's termination before returning normally.

en.statement: When Thread.sleep throws InterruptedException, it clears the current thread's interrupted status.
en.explanation: Thread.sleep reports interruption by throwing InterruptedException and clearing the interrupted status.

en.statement: A static synchronized method locks the same monitor as that class's instance synchronized methods.
en.explanation: A static synchronized method locks the declaring class's Class object. An instance synchronized method locks its receiver.

en.statement: Thread.sleep releases a monitor held by the calling thread for the duration of the sleep.
en.explanation: Thread.sleep pauses execution while the caller retains ownership of its monitors.

en.statement: Object.wait initially acquires its receiver's monitor on behalf of the calling thread.
en.explanation: Object.wait checks that the caller already owns the receiver's monitor. A caller that does not own it gets IllegalMonitorStateException.

en.statement: For a volatile int field count, `count++` performs an atomic update across threads.
en.explanation: The increment reads, adds and writes. Volatile access orders the individual accesses but does not combine them into an atomic update.

en.statement: The starting thread's writes before a successful `worker.start()` call happen-before worker's actions.
en.explanation: Program order and Thread.start establish the happens-before relation, making the starting thread's earlier writes visible to the worker.

en.statement: For a task that throws IllegalArgumentException, Future.get throws that same IllegalArgumentException.
en.explanation: Future.get reports a task's exception through ExecutionException, whose cause records the task's exception.

en.statement: After ExecutorService.shutdown, the executor rejects newly submitted tasks.
en.explanation: An orderly shutdown stops acceptance of new tasks while keeping previously submitted tasks eligible for execution.

en.statement: ExecutorService.close waits until the executor has terminated before returning.
en.explanation: ExecutorService.close initiates shutdown and waits for termination. Interruption while waiting still leads it to wait for running tasks to finish.

en.statement: A running virtual thread keeps the JVM alive after the last non-daemon thread terminates.
en.explanation: Virtual threads are daemon threads. Their continued execution does not stop JVM shutdown once the started non-daemon threads have terminated.

en.statement: Virtual threads speed up an individual task by executing its code faster than platform threads.
en.explanation: Virtual threads improve scale by accommodating more concurrent blocked tasks; they do not execute a task's code faster.

en.statement: The Java virtual threads guide recommends a reusable pool of virtual threads for task execution.
en.explanation: The Java virtual threads guide says virtual threads should never be pooled. Their low creation cost removes the reason to reuse them.

en.statement: ThreadLocal.set associates its value with the virtual thread that calls it.
en.explanation: ThreadLocal.set stores a value for the calling thread. On a virtual thread, that per-thread association belongs to the virtual thread.

en.statement: Since Java 24, a virtual thread can unmount from its carrier while blocking inside a synchronized block.
en.explanation: Holding a synchronized monitor no longer prevents a virtual thread from unmounting during a blocking operation, so that carrier can run other virtual threads.

source.title: JEP 491: Synchronize Virtual Threads without Pinning

en.statement: A virtual thread executing a native method stays pinned to its carrier for that method's duration.
en.explanation: The Java 25 virtual threads guide identifies execution of a native method as a remaining cause of carrier pinning.

en.statement: In Java 25, ScopedValue.get() returns null when its ScopedValue is unbound in the current thread.
en.explanation: ScopedValue.get throws NoSuchElementException when its key is unbound in the calling thread.

en.statement: In Java 25, ScopedValue restores the outer binding when a nested binding's operation returns.
en.explanation: When a nested ScopedValue operation returns, get observes the enclosing binding again. The inner value shadows the outer value for its operation.

en.statement: In Java 25, code in a scoped operation can replace its current ScopedValue binding in place.
en.explanation: A ScopedValue binding is immutable during its dynamic scope. ScopedValue provides no setter that overwrites that binding.

en.statement: In Java 25, a compact source file's implicitly declared class belongs to the unnamed package.
en.explanation: A compact source file places its implicitly declared class in an unnamed package; the file's grammar has no package declaration.

en.statement: In Java 25, a compact source file defines extra constructors for its implicitly declared class.
en.explanation: The compiler supplies a compact source file's class constructor. Explicit constructors for that class are excluded by the compact source file's grammar.

en.statement: In Java 25, a compact source file imports java.util.Map through its automatic java.base module import.
en.explanation: The automatic java.base module import brings exported public top-level types such as java.util.Map into scope on demand.

en.statement: In Java 25, the java launcher prefers main() over main(String[]) when both are launchable.
en.explanation: When both candidate forms exist, the launcher chooses main(String[]). Parameter count determines this choice.

en.statement: In Java 25, the java launcher creates the receiver for an instance main by invoking a zero-parameter constructor.
en.explanation: The launcher constructs the receiver for an instance main through a non-private constructor taking no arguments, then calls main on that receiver.

source.title: JEP 512: Compact Source Files and Instance Main Methods

en.statement: In Java 25, a compact source file's automatic imports include java.lang.IO.println as an unqualified method.
en.explanation: IO's static methods need a class qualifier, as in IO.println("x"), unless the source file explicitly imports those methods.

source.title: Compact Source Files and Instance main Methods

en.statement: In Java 25, `import module java.base;` works in a source file belonging to the unnamed module.
en.explanation: Module import declarations work in ordinary source files in the unnamed module. A named-module declaration is optional.

en.statement: In Java 25, module imports alone resolve the List clash between java.base and java.desktop in favor of java.base.
en.explanation: Both modules export a public type named List, so the simple name is ambiguous. An explicit import such as import java.util.List; selects the intended type.

en.statement: Since Java 22, `java Main.java` compiles a referenced sibling Helper.java when Helper.class is absent.
en.explanation: The source-file launcher locates required source files under the program's source-tree root and compiles them as needed, bringing in a referenced Helper.java.

en.statement: For code that uses preview features, javac's `--enable-preview` also enables them for a later java launch.
en.explanation: Preview features need explicit enablement during compilation and execution. The java launcher needs its own --enable-preview option for code that uses them.

en.statement: In Java 25, Structured Concurrency belongs to the finalized Java SE APIs.
en.explanation: Structured Concurrency is a preview API in Java 25. Its preview status remains subject to change in later releases.

en.statement: Oracle's Java SE Support Roadmap identifies Java SE 25 as an LTS release.
en.explanation: Oracle designates Java SE 25 for long-term support in its roadmap. LTS status describes vendor support policy.
